Probabilistic control of deterministic infrastructure

Sif is a deterministic coding substrate directed by a probabilistic planner. An LLM decides what should be done; Sif turns that decision into bounded, repeatable execution with typed plans, registered skills, validation gates, atomic promotion, durable evidence, and reusable capability memory.

Download the current ZIP | Try Sif in under a minute | Read the PDDE paper

Status: research alpha. The local-fast path is functional on the original Windows development machine. The hardened, native, CUDA, and Triton paths have additional toolchain and environment requirements. Sif is not yet a turnkey autonomous software engineer or a hosted service.

Try Sif in under a minute

The quick demonstration needs no API key and does not contact an LLM. It uses a fixed goal to stand in for the probabilistic planner so that the deterministic half of the system can be inspected by itself.

Windows: double-click try

  1. Download and extract the repository, or clone it with Git.
  2. Double-click Try-Sif.cmd.
  3. If Sif is not installed in that checkout, the launcher installs it into an isolated .venv first.
  4. Read the transaction and recovery report in the terminal window.

The demonstration performs a real operation:

  1. creates a temporary Python repository;
  2. turns a goal into a Task Envelope and typed Plan IR;
  3. resolves the registered python.add_import skill;
  4. stages and validates the exact source change;
  5. atomically promotes the passing tree;
  6. writes the transaction and evidence chain to a durable ledger; and
  7. creates a new runtime and recovers the same completed transaction from that ledger, simulating a process restart.

The temporary demonstration repository is automatically discarded. The Sif source checkout is not used as the mutation target.

Windows: double-click install

Double-click Install-Sif.cmd. The installer:

  • finds Python 3.13, 3.12, or 3.11;
  • creates .venv inside the checkout;
  • links the checkout into that environment in offline editable mode;
  • creates sif, sif-mcp, and sif-demo command shims;
  • runs an import smoke test; and
  • leaves Sif.cmd, Sif-MCP.cmd, Sif-Fuzz.cmd, and Try-Sif.cmd ready to use.

It does not add a system service, change the machine PATH, request administrator privileges, or store an API key.

Terminal equivalents

powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\install-sif.ps1
powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\try-sif.ps1

For machine-readable demonstration output:

powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\try-sif.ps1 -Json

What Sif is

Sif is not another language model. It is the implementation, validation, and memory layer beneath one.

Modern coding agents repeatedly ask a large model to emit source code, inspect the result, regenerate failing portions, and describe what happened. This is flexible, but it spends probabilistic inference on work that often becomes mechanical after the first correct solution.

Sif separates the work into two kinds:

  • Probabilistic work: understand intent, choose a strategy, decompose a novel problem, diagnose an unfamiliar failure, or propose a missing capability.
  • Deterministic work: apply known transformations, generate routine code, invoke fixed tools, compile, test, compare, benchmark, record evidence, roll back, and promote an accepted result.

    H["Human goal"] --> L["LLM planner"]
    L --> P["Typed Plan IR"]
    P --> S["Sif deterministic workers"]
    S --> V["Compilers, tests, and benchmarks"]
    V --> D{"Acceptance contract passes?"}
    D -->|"Yes"| A["Atomic promotion"]
    D -->|"No"| R["Compact repair or capability-gap packet"]
    R --> L
    A --> M["Durable evidence and capability memory"]
    M --> L
Loading

The intended deployment has one strong planner model plus Sif. The planner may delegate exceptional reasoning if its host permits it, but Sif does not require a permanent swarm of models.

The LLM becomes the vibe coder

LLMs changed human programming by allowing a person to specify intent while the model typed much of the implementation. The human became a vibe coder: a director, reviewer, and source of judgment rather than the author of every line.

Sif attempts the next move in that progression. The LLM itself becomes the vibe coder.

flowchart TB
    subgraph Today["Human-directed LLM coding"]
        H1["Human intent"] --> L1["LLM writes source tokens"]
        L1 --> H2["Human reviews and redirects"]
    end

    subgraph SifModel["LLM-directed deterministic coding"]
        H3["Human intent"] --> L2["LLM chooses a bounded plan"]
        L2 --> W["Sif writes, transforms, compiles, and tests"]
        W --> O["Deterministic evidence"]
        O --> L2
    end
Loading

The model should increasingly say things like:

Convert these three modules using the known native-migration DAG. Preserve these semantic invariants. Require differential equality, at least 1.4x speedup, and no memory regression. Return only the smallest repair packet if a gate fails.

It should not need to regenerate thousands of tokens of familiar C++, CMake, binding glue, test scaffolding, and compiler commands every time. Sif's role is to make those known operations executable and reusable.

Layer Primary responsibility
Human Desired outcome, constraints, taste, and final authority
LLM planner Interpretation, strategy, decomposition, and novel judgment
Sif Typed execution, routine code production, transactions, and replay
Compilers and tests Mechanical truth about syntax, behavior, and performance
Durable ledger What was attempted, accepted, rejected, learned, and why

The LLM remains responsible for the quality of the plan. Sif does not make an underspecified goal correct; it makes the execution of an admitted plan inspectable and repeatable.

Probabilistic direction of deterministic execution

Sif is one implementation of a broader paradigm called probabilistic direction of deterministic execution, or PDDE. The accompanying paper uses the more general phrase probabilistic control of deterministic infrastructure. The two descriptions refer to the same architectural split:

Use probabilistic intelligence where ambiguity and invention are valuable. Compile its decisions into deterministic infrastructure wherever exactness, reuse, evidence, speed, and bounded authority are valuable.

The paradigm is larger than coding. The deterministic layer could be a build system, database migration engine, laboratory instrument, deployment system, robotic controller, simulation, compliance pipeline, or defensive operations platform. In every case the probabilistic controller proposes direction while the infrastructure enforces explicit state transitions and acceptance rules.

Sif's PDDE boundary rests on several invariants:

  1. A model response is a proposal, not authority. It must parse into a bounded schema and reference admitted capabilities.
  2. Plans bind to state. Task Envelopes and Plan IR identify the repository, base snapshot, capability registry, scope, and resource limits.
  3. Execution is transactional. Work occurs in a staging tree and cannot partially leak into the accepted repository.
  4. Validation decides acceptance. Prose confidence is not a substitute for compiler, test, differential, benchmark, or policy evidence.
  5. Promotion is atomic. Either the accepted tree is promoted as one transaction or the prior state remains authoritative.
  6. Memory is explicit. Experience lives in content-addressed capabilities, receipts, event ledgers, and source-controlled primitives rather than uninspectable conversational implication.

    participant L as LLM planner
    participant P as Sif plan issuer
    participant K as Transaction kernel
    participant V as Deterministic validators
    participant E as Evidence ledger

    L->>P: Typed strategy and arguments

The important object is not just generated code. It is the tuple:

(goal, state, plan, capability versions, exact diff, validation evidence,
 approval decision, accepted state)

That tuple is what permits recovery, audit, comparison, and improvement.

How Sif learns

The word learning needs precision here. Sif 1.0 does not continuously update neural weights. Its learning is durable, symbolic, executable, and test-bound.

1. It learns reusable workflows

When the paired general coder encounters a genuine capability gap, it can ask the supervising LLM for a declarative capability made from existing trusted skills. A learned capability contains:

  • a stable learned.* identifier and content hash;
  • bounded parameters;
  • a DAG of registered skill invocations;
  • task, language, and error triggers;
  • required deterministic gates;
  • model-authored fixture invocations; and
  • concise guidance for later planner calls.

Before activation, Sif validates the schema, authority, path scope, dependencies, fixture expansion, and gates. The LLM cannot smuggle arbitrary Python, shell expressions, network access, or hidden process authority into a learned workflow.

flowchart TD
    F["Plan rejection or deterministic failure"] --> G["Typed capability gap"]
    G --> L["LLM proposes a declarative workflow"]
    L --> C["Schema, scope, DAG, and fixture validation"]
    C --> Q{"All gates pass?"}
    Q -->|"No"| X["Persist rejected candidate evidence"]
    Q -->|"Yes"| A["Activate content-addressed capability"]
    A --> R["Retry the original task"]
    R --> U["Reuse on later matching tasks"]
Loading

This learning loop may be triggered by:

  • an explicit model-declared capability gap;
  • a rejected or inadmissible plan;
  • deterministic execution failure; or
  • candidate validation failure.

A provider timeout, unavailable endpoint, or malformed transport response is not treated as a new coding capability. Availability failure is not evidence that Sif needs to learn a software operation.

2. It can acquire new core primitives

Some gaps cannot be expressed as a composition of existing skills. A new parser, CUDA lowering, compiler integration, or source transformation requires new executable code. Sif records that as an ordinary general-coding task against its own source:

analyze -> implement -> compile -> differential-test -> benchmark -> review
        -> register and atomically promote

New executable adapters are not silently loaded merely because a model wrote them. They pass the same source review, tests, artifact pinning, and registry promotion expected of other infrastructure.

3. It improves task execution through evidence

Failed candidates are not discarded as useless conversation. Sif can retain the smallest structured explanation of the failure: compiler diagnostics, failed invariants, changed paths, performance measurements, and the exact candidate identity. The planner can then revise only the failing unit instead of rereading and regenerating the entire program.

4. It learns from evolutionary evaluation

Sif can evolve bounded byte inputs against trusted in-process code or an operator-pinned executable. New behavior is retained, stable failures are minimized into content-addressed replay cases, and each sealed campaign updates target-specific mutation priors. Productive operators and seeds receive more future search effort while every operator retains an exploration floor.

When configured with the capability learner, a new failure class also emits one typed capability gap tied to its minimized replay hash. Later repetitions strengthen the evidence instead of generating duplicate model work. See Evolutionary fuzzing and outcome learning.

How Sif remembers

Sif remembers only when the operator reuses its state and catalog locations. Deleting them deliberately deletes that operational memory. There is no hidden cloud memory in the core runtime.

Memory form What it preserves Why it matters
Durable event ledger Ordered task and transaction state transitions Crash recovery, replay, and audit
Capability registry Versioned skills, schemas, artifact hashes, and status Reproducible skill resolution
Learned capability store Validated declarative workflows and their triggers Reuse without another full LLM implementation
Evidence receipts Exact diffs, snapshots, compilers, tests, metrics, and approvals Mechanical acceptance and provenance
Repair packets Bounded diagnostics tied to a failed candidate Small targeted model revisions
Fuzz learning store Target-bound operator yields, replay cases, and minimized failures Better future search and permanent regression inputs
Source-controlled primitives New deterministic implementation machinery Long-term expansion of what Sif can execute

The memory is intentionally inspectable. It is closer to a build graph, transaction log, package registry, and tested standard library than to a model's latent memory.

This also means Sif does not automatically generalize from mere exposure. A failure becomes useful only if it is represented as validated data, a reusable workflow, a new tested primitive, or evidence that changes a later plan.

Why this may reduce tokens and wall time

The economic hypothesis behind Sif is that a capable model should communicate decisions, not repeatedly spell out deterministic syntax.

For a familiar operation, the model might emit a compact typed plan containing skill IDs, paths, invariants, and thresholds. Sif can then produce or transform substantially more implementation code than the model explicitly writes. On a failure, the model receives a bounded diagnostic packet rather than every file and every build log.

Potential savings come from:

  • replacing repeated source emission with parameterized skill invocation;
  • reusing validated workflows across tasks;
  • sending only affected context and diagnostics;
  • deterministically regenerating known scaffolding;
  • parallel execution of independent plan units; and
  • avoiding model-based re-review when fixed tests can decide acceptance.

These are hypotheses to measure, not a universal 90% token-reduction claim. Fair comparisons must include planning, failed candidates, validation, revisions, tool routing, and time to an accepted result for both LLM alone and LLM + Sif.

The preliminary reports, machine-readable measurements, negative results, and token-accounting boundaries are published in the benchmark evidence index.

Current Sif 1.0 architecture

Component Function
Task Envelope Binds the goal, repository state, grants, budget, and failure policy
Typed Plan IR Describes bounded steps, dependencies, skills, and acceptance conditions
Skill ABI Defines exact inputs, outputs, authority, side effects, and versions
Capability registry Resolves active content-pinned skills and verifiers
Transaction kernel Stages work, records state, rolls back failure, and atomically promotes success
Evidence kernel Binds source, diff, toolchain, validation, approval, and accepted snapshot
Worker broker Runs fixed tools through local-fast or hardened adapters
Validation accelerator Reuses safe validation evidence and targets affected gates
Revision protocol Lets the LLM request the smallest source-bound regeneration
Capability learner Activates tested declarative compositions and records experience
Evolutionary fuzzer Searches inputs, minimizes failures, and learns target-bound operator and seed priors
MCP server Exposes planning and execution tools to an external LLM host

Serialized records continue to use some MHC names because Sif 1.0 evolved from the Modular Hierarchical Coder and must preserve its evidence ABI.

What Sif can currently work on

The checked-in capability set includes functional vertical slices for:

  • Python source inspection and deterministic edits;
  • general Python and modern C/C++ repository planning;
  • Python-to-C++ module generation and native-migration DAGs;
  • multi-module import and call lowering;
  • CMake, compiler, CTest, and differential-test orchestration;
  • CPython extensions, DLL loading, FFI, and native batch boundaries;
  • semantic Python/C++ build-graph analysis;
  • parallel module-scale code-generation workers;
  • CUDA and Triton contracts, generated kernels, compiler sandboxes, and runtime gates where the required GPU toolchains are installed;
  • compact compiler-diagnostic repair packets;
  • performance and memory acceptance gates;
  • evolutionary fuzz campaigns with replayable receipts and outcome learning; and
  • persistent MCP-directed general coding with capability learning.

Coverage is not completeness. Unsupported Python semantics, platform APIs, complex framework behavior, or novel algorithms still require planner-authored code or a new Sif primitive.

Pairing Sif with an LLM

The quick demonstration isolates Sif and uses a fixed decision. General coding requires an OpenAI-compatible planner endpoint. That planner can be local or cloud-hosted.

A loopback llama.cpp example:

.\Sif-MCP.cmd `
  --execution-profile local-fast `
  --repository C:\work\target-project `
  --repository-id repo.target-project `
  --state-root C:\sif-runtime\target-state `
  --artifact-root C:\sif-runtime\target-catalog `
  --full-catalog-source-root $PWD `
  --general-coder-endpoint http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions `
  --general-coder-model local-model `
  --general-coder-max-completion-tokens 32768 `
  --general-coder-cmake-gates `
  --general-coder-python-unittest-gate

An operator can make learned-regression replay plus bounded evolutionary fuzzing part of that same atomic promotion decision:

--general-coder-fuzz-target-id parser.frame `
--general-coder-fuzz-executable Release/frame_fuzz.exe `
--general-coder-fuzz-seed-file C:\work\corpus\valid-frame.bin `
--general-coder-fuzz-executions 10000 `
--general-coder-fuzz-wall-seconds 120 `
--general-coder-cmake-benchmark-gate

The fixed compile/test gates run first. Sif then hash-binds the candidate-built harness, replays prior failures, explores only after a clean replay, persists the sealed outcome, and either supplies compact repair evidence to the LLM or permits atomic promotion. The model cannot choose or replace the harness or its arguments through MCP. The optional benchmark flag runs CTest cases labeled benchmark after fuzzing and requires at least one such test.

An OpenRouter planner uses the exact OpenRouter endpoint and the name of an environment variable containing its token:

--general-coder-endpoint https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions `
--general-coder-model provider/model-name `
--general-coder-token-env OPENROUTER_API_KEY

The token value is not inserted into a prompt, plan, receipt, result, digest, or learned capability record.

When configured, the local-fast MCP surface includes:

  • mhc_general_code for the bounded plan, build, repair, learning, validation, and promotion loop;
  • mhc_general_coder_status for inventory and learning-state inspection;
  • mhc_local_fast_invoke for one registered skill;
  • mhc_local_fast_execute_plan for an atomic skill DAG; and
  • prepare-only inspection and planning tools inherited from the base MCP server, including inert fuzz-campaign preparation and fuzz-learning status.

See MHC_GENERAL_CODER.md and MHC_LLM_REVISION_PROTOCOL.md for the exact paired-model protocols.

Direct command-line use

Choose disjoint target, state, and catalog locations. Sif refuses overlapping protected roots.

List registered capabilities:

.\Sif.cmd `
  --repository C:\work\target-project `
  --state C:\sif-runtime\target-state `
  --repository-id repo.target-project `
  --source-root $PWD `
  --profile local-fast `
  list

Invoke one skill with typed JSON arguments:

.\Sif.cmd `
  --repository C:\work\target-project `
  --state C:\sif-runtime\target-state `
  --repository-id repo.target-project `
  --source-root $PWD `
  --profile local-fast `
  invoke `
  --skill python.add_import `
  --arguments-json '{"path":"module.py","import_statement":"import math"}' `
  --goal "Add the standard math dependency."

For complex arguments, prefer --arguments-file so the shell never rewrites the JSON.

Execution profiles

Profile Intended use Boundary
local-fast Trusted, single-owner development machine In-process deterministic adapters and automatic exact-diff approval; validation, transactions, and rollback remain enabled
hardened Unknown code, shared systems, or security-sensitive promotion AppContainer and authenticated compiler/project evidence where configured
prepare-only External executor or review workflow Produces bounded tasks and plans without mutation authority

Local-fast is the normal workstation profile. It is not a hostile-code containment claim. Hardened mode intentionally fails closed when the operating system cannot reproduce security metadata exactly.

Requirements

For the one-click demonstration:

  • Windows 10 or 11;
  • PowerShell 5.1 or newer; and
  • Python 3.11, 3.12, or 3.13.

For broader native coding:

  • Visual Studio Build Tools and the Windows SDK;
  • CMake and Ninja;
  • Clang/LLVM where Clang validation is selected; and
  • optional CUDA Toolkit, compatible PyTorch, and Triton installations for GPU workflows.

The core contracts, registry, deterministic rewrites, quick demonstration, and many planning functions use the Python standard library. Native and GPU features activate only when their runtimes are configured.

Development setup

The double-click installer can include test dependencies:

powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\install-sif.ps1 -WithDev
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest -q

Manual setup is equivalent:

py -3.13 -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"
python -m pytest -q

The canonical console commands are sif, sif-mcp, sif-fuzz, and sif-demo. Legacy mhc, mhc-mcp, and mhc-fuzz aliases remain available for compatibility.

Repository layout

  • hierarchical_coder/ - Sif runtime, contracts, workers, fixtures, and design documents
  • examples/ - executable, no-key quick demonstration
  • scripts/ - one-click installer and try implementation
  • tools/ - operator CLIs, MCP launcher, audits, and benchmarks
  • tests/ - deterministic, security, native, CUDA/Triton, and integration tests
  • native_skill_runtime.cpp - native skill runtime reference
  • native_rewrite_cpp_ext.py - native rewrite extension integration
  • MHC_SHOWTIME_READINESS.md - detailed readiness and limitations report

Security and trust

Generated source, model responses, repository text, compiler diagnostics, and test output are untrusted inputs. A capable planner is not a reason to weaken path grants, artifact pins, diff binding, deterministic gates, or transaction boundaries.

Read SECURITY.md, the checked-in threat model, and MHC_HARDENED_RUNTIME_INTEGRATION.md before using Sif against unknown code or shared infrastructure.

Current boundaries

Sif 1.0 does not yet guarantee that:

  • every Python program can be translated into correct and faster C++;
  • every model emits an admissible Plan IR on its first attempt;
  • every repository has sufficient tests to define correctness;
  • learned workflow compositions can replace a genuinely missing primitive;
  • GPU code will compile without a compatible local CUDA/Triton stack;
  • deterministic code generation is automatically faster than handwritten expert code; or
  • token reduction in one benchmark generalizes to every coding task.

The effective ceiling is the combination of human specification, planner quality, available context, registered primitives, toolchains, and acceptance oracles. Sif makes that boundary explicit and improvable.

Naming and compatibility

Sif 1.0 is the product and repository name. MHC is the original implementation namespace and remains in Python modules, commands, JSON schemas, receipts, and documentation where changing it would break existing evidence or integrations. A future versioned migration can introduce new serialized names without falsifying old receipts.

It learns reusable workflows When the paired general coder encounters a genuine capability gap, it can ask the supervising LLM for a declarative capability made from existing trusted skills. A learned capability contains: a stable learned.* identifier and content hash; bounded parameters; a DAG of registered skill invocations; task, language, and error triggers; required deterministic gates; model-authored fixture invocations; and concise guidance for later planner calls. Before activation, Sif validates the schema, authority, path scope, dependencies, fixture expansion, and gates. The LLM cannot smuggle arbitrary Python, shell expressions, network access, or hidden process authority into a learned workflow. flowchart TD F["Plan rejection or deterministic failure"] --> G["Typed capability gap"] G --> L["LLM proposes a declarative workflow"] L --> C["Schema, scope, DAG, and fixture validation"] C --> Q{"All gates pass?"} Q -->|"No"| X["Persist rejected candidate evidence"] Q -->|"Yes"| A["Activate content-addressed capability"] A --> R["Retry the original task"] R --> U["Reuse on later matching tasks"] Loading This learning loop may be triggered by: an explicit model-declared capability gap; a rejected or inadmissible plan; deterministic execution failure; or candidate validation failure. A provider timeout, unavailable endpoint, or malformed transport response is not treated as a new coding capability. Availability failure is not evidence that Sif needs to learn a software operation. 2. It can acquire new core primitives Some gaps cannot be expressed as a composition of existing skills. A new parser, CUDA lowering, compiler integration, or source transformation requires new executable code. Sif records that as an ordinary general-coding task against its own source: analyze -> implement -> compile -> differential-test -> benchmark -> review -> register and atomically promote New executable adapters are not silently loaded merely because a model wrote them. They pass the same source review, tests, artifact pinning, and registry promotion expected of other infrastructure. 3. It improves task execution through evidence Failed candidates are not discarded as useless conversation. Sif can retain the smallest structured explanation of the failure: compiler diagnostics, failed invariants, changed paths, performance measurements, and the exact candidate identity. The planner can then revise only the failing unit instead of rereading and regenerating the entire program. 4. It learns from evolutionary evaluation Sif can evolve bounded byte inputs against trusted in-process code or an operator-pinned executable. New behavior is retained, stable failures are minimized into content-addressed replay cases, and each sealed campaign updates target-specific mutation priors. Productive operators and seeds receive more future search effort while every operator retains an exploration floor. When configured with the capability learner, a new failure class also emits one typed capability gap tied to its minimized replay hash. Later repetitions strengthen the evidence instead of generating duplicate model work. See Evolutionary fuzzing and outcome learning. How Sif remembers Sif remembers only when the operator reuses its state and catalog locations. Deleting them deliberately deletes that operational memory. There is no hidden cloud memory in the core runtime. Memory form What it preserves Why it matters Durable event ledger Ordered task and transaction state transitions Crash recovery, replay, and audit Capability registry Versioned skills, schemas, artifact hashes, and status Reproducible skill resolution Learned capability store Validated declarative workflows and their triggers Reuse without another full LLM implementation Evidence receipts Exact diffs, snapshots, compilers, tests, metrics, and approvals Mechanical acceptance and provenance Repair packets Bounded diagnostics tied to a failed candidate Small targeted model revisions Fuzz learning store Target-bound operator yields, replay cases, and minimized failures Better future search and permanent regression inputs Source-controlled primitives New deterministic implementation machinery Long-term expansion of what Sif can execute The memory is intentionally inspectable. It is closer to a build graph, transaction log, package registry, and tested standard library than to a model's latent memory. This also means Sif does not automatically generalize from mere exposure. A failure becomes useful only if it is represented as validated data, a reusable workflow, a new tested primitive, or evidence that changes a later plan. Why this may reduce tokens and wall time The economic hypothesis behind Sif is that a capable model should communicate decisions, not repeatedly spell out deterministic syntax. For a familiar operation, the model might emit a compact typed plan containing skill IDs, paths, invariants, and thresholds. Sif can then produce or transform substantially more implementation code than the model explicitly writes. On a failure, the model receives a bounded diagnostic packet rather than every file and every build log. Potential savings come from: replacing repeated source emission with parameterized skill invocation; reusing validated workflows across tasks; sending only affected context and diagnostics; deterministically regenerating known scaffolding; parallel execution of independent plan units; and avoiding model-based re-review when fixed tests can decide acceptance. These are hypotheses to measure, not a universal 90% token-reduction claim. Fair comparisons must include planning, failed candidates, validation, revisions, tool routing, and time to an accepted result for both LLM alone and LLM + Sif. The preliminary reports, machine-readable measurements, negative results, and token-accounting boundaries are published in the benchmark evidence index. Current Sif 1.0 architecture Component Function Task Envelope Binds the goal, repository state, grants, budget, and failure policy Typed Plan IR Describes bounded steps, dependencies, skills, and acceptance conditions Skill ABI Defines exact inputs, outputs, authority, side effects, and versions Capability registry Resolves active content-pinned skills and verifiers Transaction kernel Stages work, records state, rolls back failure, and atomically promotes success Evidence kernel Binds source, diff, toolchain, validation, approval, and accepted snapshot Worker broker Runs fixed tools through local-fast or hardened adapters Validation accelerator Reuses safe validation evidence and targets affected gates Revision protocol Lets the LLM request the smallest source-bound regeneration Capability learner Activates tested declarative compositions and records experience Evolutionary fuzzer Searches inputs, minimizes failures, and learns target-bound operator and seed priors MCP server Exposes planning and execution tools to an external LLM host Serialized records continue to use some MHC names because Sif 1.0 evolved from the Modular Hierarchical Coder and must preserve its evidence ABI. What Sif can currently work on The checked-in capability set includes functional vertical slices for: Python source inspection and deterministic edits; general Python and modern C/C++ repository planning; Python-to-C++ module generation and native-migration DAGs; multi-module import and call lowering; CMake, compiler, CTest, and differential-test orchestration; CPython extensions, DLL loading, FFI, and native batch boundaries; semantic Python/C++ build-graph analysis; parallel module-scale code-generation workers; CUDA and Triton contracts, generated kernels, compiler sandboxes, and runtime gates where the required GPU toolchains are installed; compact compiler-diagnostic repair packets; performance and memory acceptance gates; evolutionary fuzz campaigns with replayable receipts and outcome learning; and persistent MCP-directed general coding with capability learning. Coverage is not completeness. Unsupported Python semantics, platform APIs, complex framework behavior, or novel algorithms still require planner-authored code or a new Sif primitive. Pairing Sif with an LLM The quick demonstration isolates Sif and uses a fixed decision. General coding requires an OpenAI-compatible planner endpoint. That planner can be local or cloud-hosted. A loopback llama.cpp example: .\Sif-MCP.cmd ` --execution-profile local-fast ` --repository C:\work\target-project ` --repository-id repo.target-project ` --state-root C:\sif-runtime\target-state ` --artifact-root C:\sif-runtime\target-catalog ` --full-catalog-source-root $PWD ` --general-coder-endpoint http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions ` --general-coder-model local-model ` --general-coder-max-completion-tokens 32768 ` --general-coder-cmake-gates ` --general-coder-python-unittest-gate An operator can make learned-regression replay plus bounded evolutionary fuzzing part of that same atomic promotion decision: --general-coder-fuzz-target-id parser.frame ` --general-coder-fuzz-executable Release/frame_fuzz.exe ` --general-coder-fuzz-seed-file C:\work\corpus\valid-frame.bin ` --general-coder-fuzz-executions 10000 ` --general-coder-fuzz-wall-seconds 120 ` --general-coder-cmake-benchmark-gate The fixed compile/test gates run first. Sif then hash-binds the candidate-built harness, replays prior failures, explores only after a clean replay, persists the sealed outcome, and either supplies compact repair evidence to the LLM or permits atomic promotion. The model cannot choose or replace the harness or its arguments through MCP. The optional benchmark flag runs CTest cases labeled benchmark after fuzzing and requires at least one such test. An OpenRouter planner uses the exact OpenRouter endpoint and the name of an environment variable containing its token: --general-coder-endpoint https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions ` --general-coder-model provider/model-name ` --general-coder-token-env OPENROUTER_API_KEY The token value is not inserted into a prompt, plan, receipt, result, digest, or learned capability record. When configured, the local-fast MCP surface includes: mhc_general_code for the bounded plan, build, repair, learning, validation, and promotion loop; mhc_general_coder_status for inventory and learning-state inspection; mhc_local_fast_invoke for one registered skill; mhc_local_fast_execute_plan for an atomic skill DAG; and prepare-only inspection and planning tools inherited from the base MCP server, including inert fuzz-campaign preparation and fuzz-learning status. See MHC_GENERAL_CODER.md and MHC_LLM_REVISION_PROTOCOL.md for the exact paired-model protocols. Direct command-line use Choose disjoint target, state, and catalog locations. Sif refuses overlapping protected roots. List registered capabilities: .\Sif.cmd ` --repository C:\work\target-project ` --state C:\sif-runtime\target-state ` --repository-id repo.target-project ` --source-root $PWD ` --profile local-fast ` list Invoke one skill with typed JSON arguments: .\Sif.cmd ` --repository C:\work\target-project ` --state C:\sif-runtime\target-state ` --repository-id repo.target-project ` --source-root $PWD ` --profile local-fast ` invoke ` --skill python.add_import ` --arguments-json '{"path":"module.py","import_statement":"import math"}' ` --goal "Add the standard math dependency." For complex arguments, prefer --arguments-file so the shell never rewrites the JSON. Execution profiles Profile Intended use Boundary local-fast Trusted, single-owner development machine In-process deterministic adapters and automatic exact-diff approval; validation, transactions, and rollback remain enabled hardened Unknown code, shared systems, or security-sensitive promotion AppContainer and authenticated compiler/project evidence where configured prepare-only External executor or review workflow Produces bounded tasks and plans without mutation authority Local-fast is the normal workstation profile. It is not a hostile-code containment claim. Hardened mode intentionally fails closed when the operating system cannot reproduce security metadata exactly. Requirements For the one-click demonstration: Windows 10 or 11; PowerShell 5.1 or newer; and Python 3.11, 3.12, or 3.13. For broader native coding: Visual Studio Build Tools and the Windows SDK; CMake and Ninja; Clang/LLVM where Clang validation is selected; and optional CUDA Toolkit, compatible PyTorch, and Triton installations for GPU workflows. The core contracts, registry, deterministic rewrites, quick demonstration, and many planning functions use the Python standard library. Native and GPU features activate only when their runtimes are configured. Development setup The double-click installer can include test dependencies: powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\install-sif.ps1 -WithDev .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest -q Manual setup is equivalent: py -3.13 -m venv .venv .\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 python -m pip install -e ".[dev]" python -m pytest -q The canonical console commands are sif, sif-mcp, sif-fuzz, and sif-demo. Legacy mhc, mhc-mcp, and mhc-fuzz aliases remain available for compatibility. Repository layout hierarchical_coder/ - Sif runtime, contracts, workers, fixtures, and design documents examples/ - executable, no-key quick demonstration scripts/ - one-click installer and try implementation tools/ - operator CLIs, MCP launcher, audits, and benchmarks tests/ - deterministic, security, native, CUDA/Triton, and integration tests native_skill_runtime.cpp - native skill runtime reference native_rewrite_cpp_ext.py - native rewrite extension integration MHC_SHOWTIME_READINESS.md - detailed readiness and limitations report Security and trust Generated source, model responses, repository text, compiler diagnostics, and test output are untrusted inputs. A capable planner is not a reason to weaken path grants, artifact pins, diff binding, deterministic gates, or transaction boundaries. Read SECURITY.md, the checked-in threat model, and MHC_HARDENED_RUNTIME_INTEGRATION.md before using Sif against unknown code or shared infrastructure. Current boundaries Sif 1.0 does not yet guarantee that: every Python program can be translated into correct and faster C++; every model emits an admissible Plan IR on its first attempt; every repository has sufficient tests to define correctness; learned workflow compositions can replace a genuinely missing primitive; GPU code will compile without a compatible local CUDA/Triton stack; deterministic code generation is automatically faster than handwritten expert code; or token reduction in one benchmark generalizes to every coding task. The effective ceiling is the combination of human specification, planner quality, available context, registered primitives, toolchains, and acceptance oracles. Sif makes that boundary explicit and improvable. Naming and compatibility Sif 1.0 is the product and repository name. MHC is the original implementation namespace and remains in Python modules, commands, JSON schemas, receipts, and documentation where changing it would break existing evidence or integrations. A future versioned migration can introduce new serialized names without falsifying old receipts. blocks.html_en: • A model response is a proposal, not authority. It must parse into a bounded schema and reference admitted capabilities.

blocks.html_en: • Plans bind to state. Task Envelopes and Plan IR identify the repository, base snapshot, capability registry, scope, and resource limits.

sentences.en: Prose confidence is not a substitute for compiler, test, differential, benchmark, or policy evidence.
sentences.zh: 散文信心不能替代编译器、测试、差异、基准或政策证据。

sentences.en: Either the accepted tree is promoted as one transaction or the prior state remains authoritative.
sentences.zh: 要么将接受的树作为一笔交易进行提升，要么先前的状态保持权威。

content_html_zh:
确定性基础设施的概率控制

Sif 是由概率规划器指导的确定性编码基底。 法学硕士决定应该做什么； Sif 通过类型化计划、注册技能、验证门、原子提升、持久证据和可重用能力内存，将该决策转化为有界、可重复的执行。

下载当前 ZIP |一分钟内试用 Sif |阅读 PDDE 论文

状态：研究阿尔法。 本地快速路径可在原始 Windows 开发计算机上运行。 硬化、本机、CUDA 和 Triton 路径有额外的工具链和环境要求。 Sif 还不是交钥匙自主软件工程师或托管服务。

一分钟内试用 Sif

快速演示不需要 API 密钥，也不需要联系法学硕士。 它使用固定目标来代替概率规划器，以便可以自行检查系统的确定性部分。

Windows：双击尝试

  1. 下载并解压存储库，或使用 Git 克隆它。
  2. 双击 Try-Sif.cmd。
  3. 如果该签出中未安装 Sif，启动器将首先将其安装到隔离的 .venv 中。
  4. 在终端窗口中阅读事务和恢复报告。

演示执行实际操作：

  1. 创建一个临时Python存储库；
  2. 将目标转化为任务信封并输入 Plan IR；
  3. 解析已注册的python.add_import技能；
  4. 阶段并验证确切的源更改；
  5. 原子地提升传递树；
  6. 将交易和证据链写入持久账本；和
  7. 创建一个新的运行时并从该分类账中恢复相同的已完成事务，模拟流程重新启动。

临时演示存储库将被自动丢弃。 Sif 源 checkout 不用作突变目标。

Windows：双击安装

双击Install-Sif.cmd。 安装程序：

  • 查找 Python 3.13、3.12 或 3.11；
  • 在结帐内创建 .venv；
  • 以离线可编辑模式将结帐链接到该环境；
  • 创建 sif、sif-mcp 和 sif-demo 命令垫片；
  • 进行进口冒烟测试；和
  • 使 Sif.cmd、Sif-MCP.cmd、Sif-Fuzz.cmd 和 Try-Sif.cmd 可供使用。

它不会添加系统服务、更改计算机路径、请求管理员权限或存储 API 密钥。

终端等效项

powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\install-sif.ps1
powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\try-sif.ps1

对于机器可读的演示输出：

powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\try-sif.ps1 -Json

西芙是什么

Sif 不是另一种语言模型。 它是下面一层的实现、验证和存储层。

现代编码代理反复要求大型模型发出源代码、检查结果、重新生成失败部分并描述发生的情况。 这是灵活的，但它在工作上花费了概率推理，而在第一个正确的解决方案之后，这些工作往往变得机械化。

Sif 将作品分为两种：

  • 概率工作：理解意图、选择策略、分解新问题、诊断不熟悉的故障或提出缺失的功能。
  • 确定性工作：应用已知的转换、生成常规代码、调用固定工具、编译、测试、比较、基准测试、记录证据、回滚并提升可接受的结果。

预期的部署有一个强大的规划器模型加上 Sif。 如果主机允许，规划器可以委托特殊推理，但 Sif 不需要永久的模型群。

法学硕士成为振动编码员

法学硕士改变了人类编程，允许人们指定意图，而模型键入大部分实现。 人类成为了一名氛围编码员：导演、审稿人和判断的来源，而不是每一行的作者。

Sif 尝试该进程中的下一步。 法学硕士本身就成为了振动编码器。

该模型应该越来越多地表述如下内容：

使用已知的本机迁移 DAG 转换这三个模块。 保留这些语义不变量。 要求微分相等、至少 1.4 倍加速，并且无内存回归。 如果门发生故障，则仅返回最小的修复包。

它不需要每次都重新生成数千个熟悉的 C++、CMake、绑定胶水、测试脚手架和编译器命令的标记。 Sif 的作用是使那些已知的操作可执行并可重用。

Layer 主要责任
Human 期望的结果、限制、品味和最终权威
法学硕士规划师 解释、策略、分解和新颖的判断

法学硕士仍然对计划的质量负责。 Sif 不会使未明确的目标变得正确；它使已承认的计划的执行可检查且可重复。

确定性执行的概率方向

Sif 是一种更广泛范式的实现，称为确定性执行的概率方向（PDDE）。 随附的论文使用了更通用的短语“确定性基础设施的概率控制”。 这两个描述指的是相同的架构划分：

在模糊性和创造性有价值的地方使用概率智能。 在准确性、重用性、证据、速度和有限权限有价值的情况下，将其决策编译成确定性基础设施。

范式比编码更大。 确定性层可以是构建系统、数据库迁移引擎、实验室仪器、部署系统、机器人控制器、模拟、合规管道或防御操作平台。 在每种情况下，概率控制器都会提出方向，而基础设施则强制执行明确的状态转换和接受规则。

Sif 的 PDDE 边界取决于几个不变量：

  1. 模范回应是建议，而不是权威。 它必须解析为有界模式并引用承认的功能。
  2. 计划受国家约束。 任务信封和计划 IR 确定存储库、基本快照、功能注册表、范围和资源限制。
  3. 执行是事务性的。 工作发生在临时树中，不能部分泄漏到接受的存储库中。
  4. 验证决定接受。 散文信心不能替代编译器、测试、差异、基准或政策证据。
  5. 促销是原子的。 要么将接受的树作为一笔交易进行提升，要么先前的状态保持权威。
  6. 记忆是外显的。 体验存在于内容寻址功能、收据、事件分类帐和源控制原语中，而不是无法检查的对话含义中。

重要的对象不仅仅是生成的代码。 它是元组：

西芙如何学习

学习这个词在这里需要精确。 Sif 1.0 不会持续更新神经权重。 它的学习是持久的、象征性的、可执行的和受测试约束的。

1. 它学习可重用的工作流程

当配对的普通编码员遇到真正的能力差距时，它可以向监督法学硕士请求根据现有可信技能制定的声明性能力。 学习到的能力包含：

  • 稳定的学习.* 标识符和内容哈希；
  • 有界参数；
  • 注册技能调用的 DAG；
  • 任务、语言和错误触发器；
  • 所需的确定性门；
  • 模型创作的夹具调用；和
  • 为以后的计划者通话提供简洁的指导。

在激活之前，Sif 会验证模式、权限、路径范围、依赖项、夹具扩展和门。 LLM 无法将任意 Python、shell 表达式、网络访问或隐藏进程权限偷偷带入学习的工作流程中。

flowchart TD
    F["Plan rejection or deterministic failure"] --> G["Typed capability gap"]
    G --> L["LLM proposes a declarative workflow"]
    L --> C["Schema, scope, DAG, and fixture validation"]
    C --> Q{"All gates pass?"}
    Q -->|"No"| X["Persist rejected candidate evidence"]
    Q -->|"Yes"| A["Activate content-addressed capability"]
    A --> R["Retry the original task"]
    R --> U["Reuse on later matching tasks"]
Loading

这个学习循环可能由以下因素触发：

  • 明确的模型声明的能力差距；
  • 被拒绝或不可接受的计划；
  • 确定性执行失败；或者
  • 候选验证失败。

提供程序超时、不可用端点或格式错误的传输响应不会被视为新的编码功能。 可用性失败并不表明 Sif 需要学习软件操作。

2. 它可以获得新的核心原语

有些差距不能用现有技能的组合来表示。 新的解析器、CUDA 降低、编译器集成或源转换需要新的可执行代码。 Sif 将其记录为针对其自己的源的普通通用编码任务：

analyze -> implement -> compile -> differential-test -> benchmark -> review
        -> register and atomically promote

新的可执行适配器不会仅仅因为模型编写了它们而被静默加载。 它们通过了与其他基础设施相同的源审查、测试、工件固定和注册表升级。

3. 它通过证据改善任务执行

失败的候选人不会因为无用的谈话而被丢弃。 Sif 可以保留对失败的最小结构化解释：编译器诊断、失败的不变量、更改的路径、性能测量以及确切的候选身份。 然后，规划者可以仅修改失败的单元，而不是重新读取和重新生成整个程序。

4. 它从进化评估中学习

Sif 可以针对受信任的进程内代码或操作员固定的可执行文件演化有界字节输入。 新的行为被保留，稳定的失败被最小化到内容寻址的重播案例中，并且每个密封的活动都会更新目标特定的突变先验。 高效的运营商和种子将在未来获得更多的搜索工作，而每个运营商都保留一个勘探层。

当配置了能力学习器时，新的故障类还会发出与其最小化重放哈希相关的一种类型化能力差距。 后来的重复加强了证据，而不是产生重复的模型工作。 请参阅进化模糊测试和结果学习。

西芙如何记得

仅当操作员重用其状态和目录位置时，Sif 才会记住。 故意删除它们会删除该操作内存。 核心运行时中没有隐藏的云内存。

记忆形式 它保留了什么 为什么这很重要
耐用的事件分类账 有序任务和事务状态转换 崩溃恢复、重放和审核
能力登记 版本化技能、模式、工件哈希和状态 可重复的技能分辨率
学习能力存储 经过验证的声明式工作流程及其触发器 无需再次实施完整的 LLM 即可重复使用
证据收据 精确的差异、快照、编译器、测试、指标和批准 机械验收和出处
维修包 与失败的候选者相关的有限诊断 小规模目标模型修改
模糊学习商店 目标绑定算子产量、重放案例和最小化故障 更好的未来搜索和永久回归输入
源代码控制原语 新的确定性实施机制 长期扩展 Sif 的执行能力

内存是有意检查的。 它更接近构建图、事务日志、包注册表和经过测试的标准库，而不是模型的潜在内存。

这也意味着 Sif 不会自动从单纯的曝光中进行概括。 仅当失败被表示为经过验证的数据、可重用的工作流程、新的经过测试的原语或更改后续计划的证据时，它才变得有用。

为什么这可以减少令牌和占用时间

Sif 背后的经济假设是，一个有能力的模型应该传达决策，而不是重复地阐明确定性语法。

对于熟悉的操作，模型可能会发出一个紧凑的类型计划，其中包含技能 ID、路径、不变量和阈值。 然后，Sif 可以生成或转换比模型显式编写的更多的实现代码。 发生故障时，模型会收到有限的诊断数据包，而不是每个文件和每个构建日志。

潜在的节省来自：

  • 用参数化技能调用替换重复的源发射；
  • 跨任务重用经过验证的工作流程；
  • 仅发送受影响的上下文和诊断信息；
  • 确定性地再生已知的脚手架；
  • 独立计划单元的并行执行；和
  • 当固定测试可以决定是否接受时，避免基于模型的重新审查。

这些是需要衡量的假设，而不是普遍的 90% 代币减少主张。 公平比较必须包括单独 LLM 和 LLM + Sif 的计划、失败的候选人、验证、修订、工具路由以及获得可接受结果的时间。

初步报告、机器可读的测量结果、负面结果和代币会计边界均发布在基准证据索引中。

将 Sif 与法学硕士配对

快速演示隔离了 Sif 并使用固定决策。 一般编码需要兼容 OpenAI 的规划器端点。 该规划器可以是本地的或云托管的。

环回 llama.cpp 示例：

.\Sif-MCP.cmd `
  --execution-profile local-fast `
  --repository C:\work\target-project `
  --repository-id repo.target-project `
  --state-root C:\sif-runtime\target-state `
  --artifact-root C:\sif-runtime\target-catalog `
  --full-catalog-source-root $PWD `
  --general-coder-endpoint http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions `
  --general-coder-model local-model `
  --general-coder-max-completion-tokens 32768 `
  --general-coder-cmake-gates `
  --general-coder-python-unittest-gate

操作员可以将学习回归重放加上有界进化模糊测试作为同一原子升级决策的一部分：

--general-coder-fuzz-target-id parser.frame `
--general-coder-fuzz-executable Release/frame_fuzz.exe `
--general-coder-fuzz-seed-file C:\work\corpus\valid-frame.bin `
--general-coder-fuzz-executions 10000 `
--general-coder-fuzz-wall-seconds 120 `
--general-coder-cmake-benchmark-gate

固定的编译/测试门首先运行。 然后，Sif 哈希绑定候选构建的工具，重放之前的故障，仅在干净重放后进行探索，保留密封结果，并向 LLM 提供紧凑的修复证据或允许原子升级。 模型无法通过 MCP 选择或替换线束或其参数。 可选的基准标记在模糊测试后运行标记为基准的 CTest 用例，并且需要至少一项此类测试。

OpenRouter 规划器使用确切的 OpenRouter 端点和包含其令牌的环境变量的名称：

--general-coder-endpoint https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions `
--general-coder-model provider/model-name `
--general-coder-token-env OPENROUTER_API_KEY

令牌值不会插入到提示、计划、收据、结果、摘要或学习能力记录中。

配置后，本地快速 MCP 表面包括：

  • mhc_general_code 用于有界计划、构建、修复、学习、验证和升级循环；
  • mhc_general_coder_status 用于库存和学习状态检查；
  • mhc_local_fast_invoke 用于一项注册技能；
  • mhc_local_fast_execute_plan 用于原子技能 DAG；和
  • 从基础 MCP 服务器继承的仅准备检查和规划工具，包括惰性模糊活动准备和模糊学习状态。

有关确切的配对模型协议，请参阅 MHC_GENERAL_CODER.md 和 MHC_LLM_REVISION_PROTOCOL.md。

直接命令行使用

选择不相交的目标、状态和目录位置。 Sif 拒绝重叠受保护的根。

列出已注册的功能：

.\Sif.cmd `
  --repository C:\work\target-project `
  --state C:\sif-runtime\target-state `
  --repository-id repo.target-project `
  --source-root $PWD `
  --profile local-fast `
  list

使用类型化 JSON 参数调用一项技能：

.\Sif.cmd `
  --repository C:\work\target-project `
  --state C:\sif-runtime\target-state `
  --repository-id repo.target-project `
  --source-root $PWD `
  --profile local-fast `
  invoke `
  --skill python.add_import `
  --arguments-json '{"path":"module.py","import_statement":"import math"}' `
  --goal "Add the standard math dependency."

对于复杂的参数，最好使用 --arguments-file，这样 shell 就不会重写 JSON。

安全与信任

生成的源、模型响应、存储库文本、编译器诊断和测试输出是不受信任的输入。 有能力的规划者并不是削弱路径授权、工件引脚、差异绑定、确定性门或事务边界的理由。

在针对未知代码或共享基础设施使用 Sif 之前，请阅读 SECURITY.md、签入的威胁模型和 MHC_HARDENED_RUNTIME_INTEGRATION.md。

当前边界

Sif 1.0 尚不保证：

  • 每个Python程序都可以被翻译成正确且更快的C++；
  • 每个模型在第一次尝试时都会发出可接受的 Plan IR；
  • 每个存储库都有足够的测试来定义正确性；
  • 学习的工作流程组合可以替换真正缺失的基元；
  • GPU 代码无需兼容的本地 CUDA/Triton 堆栈即可编译；
  • 确定性代码生成自动比手写专家代码更快；或者
  • 一个基准测试中的标记减少可以推广到每一项编码任务。

有效上限是人类规范、规划者质量、​​可用上下文、注册原语、工具链和接受预言的组合。 Sif 使该界限变得明确且可改进。

命名和兼容性

Sif 1.0 是产品和存储库名称。 MHC 是原始实现命名空间，保留在 Python 模块、命令、JSON 模式、收据和文档中，更改它会破坏现有证据或集成。 未来的版本化迁移可以引入新的序列化名称，而不会伪造旧的收据。
